A currency is a system of money in common use within a specific environment over time, especially for people in a nation state. It is typically issued and controlled by a central bank or monetary authority and serves as a medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value.

The process of changing something from one form to another. Currency conversion refers to exchanging an amount of money in one currency for the equivalent value in another currency, typically using an exchange rate.

The price at which a buyer is willing to purchase a currency or other asset. In a quoted currency pair, the bid is the lower of the two prices and represents what a dealer will pay to buy the base currency.

The price at which a seller is willing to sell a currency or other asset. In a quoted currency pair, the ask is the higher of the two prices and represents what a dealer will accept to sell the base currency.

The difference between two prices, rates, or yields. In foreign exchange, the bid-ask spread is the difference between the ask price (at which a dealer sells) and the bid price (at which a dealer buys), and represents a transaction cost.

In a currency pair, the quote currency (also called the counter currency) is the second currency listed and indicates how much of it is required to buy one unit of the base currency. For example, in EUR/USD, USD is the quote currency.

Relating to a future date. A forward exchange rate is the rate agreed today for a currency transaction to be settled on a specified future date, derived from the spot rate and the interest rate differential between the two currencies.
A spot transaction is a foreign exchange deal in which two parties agree to exchange currencies at the current market rate, with settlement typically occurring within two business days.
The intended destination or endpoint of a process. In a currency conversion, the target side refers to the currency being converted into.

Financial instruments are monetary contracts between parties. In foreign exchange markets, the main instruments include spot transactions, outright forwards, foreign exchange swaps, currency swaps, and options.

The euro (symbol: €; currency code: EUR) is the official currency of 21 of the 27 member states of the European Union. This group of states is officially known as the euro area, more commonly named the eurozone. The euro is divided into 100 euro cents.

The yen (symbol: ¥; currency code: JPY) is the official currency of Japan. It is the third most-traded currency in the foreign exchange market after the United States dollar and the euro, and is widely used as a reserve currency. The yen is divided into 100 sen, though sen are no longer used in everyday transactions.

The renminbi (symbol: ¥; currency code: CNY; abbreviation: RMB) is the official currency of the People's Republic of China. Its primary unit is the yuan. Issued by the People's Bank of China, the renminbi is one of the world's most-traded currencies and is included in the IMF's Special Drawing Rights basket.

A residual category used to group together items that are not individually itemised. In currency turnover statistics, 'other currencies' aggregates the trading volume of all currencies outside the top-ranked ones.
A value that remains after specified deductions or adjustments. In foreign exchange turnover statistics, 'net' refers to adjustments removing double-counting between reporting dealers.

A completed agreement between a buyer and a seller to exchange goods, services, or financial instruments. In foreign exchange, a transaction typically involves the exchange of one currency for another at an agreed rate.

An outright forward is a foreign exchange contract obliging two parties to exchange currencies at a specified rate on a future date beyond the spot settlement window. It differs from a swap in that it consists of a single leg rather than two.

Forward contracts are agreements to buy or sell an asset at a predetermined price on a specified future date. Currency forwards are widely used to hedge foreign exchange risk arising from future cash flows in foreign currencies.

A currency swap (or FX swap) is a foreign exchange transaction that combines a spot purchase or sale of a currency with a simultaneous forward sale or purchase of the same currency. It is widely used to manage liquidity and hedge foreign exchange exposure.

A foreign exchange option gives the holder the right, but not the obligation, to exchange one currency for another at a specified rate on or before a specified date. Options are typically used to hedge or to speculate on currency movements.
